questions.prompt: What does a Cirq qubit object provide?
questions.explanation: Cirq operations target explicit qubit objects such as LineQubit(0).

questions.prompt: What is a moment in Cirq?

options.text: A time slice of compatible operations

questions.explanation: Moments organize operations that can occupy the same circuit time slice.

questions.prompt: Which call produces repeated classical measurements?
questions.explanation: Simulator.run samples the circuit repeatedly when measurement operations are present.

questions.prompt: What does simulate provide for an unmeasured ideal circuit?

options.text: An exact final state under a declared order

questions.explanation: simulate exposes the internal ideal state, while run is used for repeated measurement records.

questions.prompt: Why pass qubit_order=[q1,q0] in the asymmetric example?

options.text: To choose the tensor-factor order for the state array

questions.explanation: Explicit order maps statevector indices to the intended q1q0 convention.

options.text: The classical record order under the key

questions.explanation: The measurement argument order controls how the recorded bits are interpreted; it does not insert a quantum SWAP.

questions.prompt: What can happen if an idle q1 is omitted from qubit_order?

options.text: The returned state can have the wrong dimension

questions.explanation: An omitted idle wire may disappear from the active tensor space, preventing a fair two-qubit comparison.

questions.prompt: Why can a symmetric Bell histogram fail to expose reversed bit order?

options.text: 00 and 11 remain the same under the reversal

questions.explanation: The Bell support is symmetric. An asymmetric X(q0) fixture is a better ordering test.

questions.prompt: What should a cross-framework comparison do before comparing finite counts?

options.text: Normalize logical gates and basis order, then compare ideal probabilities
Force every library to use the same API
Add SWAP gates until strings match
Assume the first histogram is correct

questions.explanation: A staged comparison separates logical, representational and statistical differences.
